title: Math Worksheet Generator
empty_hint: Pick a topic, adjust the controls, then press Generate to create a worksheet.
mixed_operations_p: Practice mixed operations and order of operations.
geometry_p: Calculate area and perimeter of shapes
linear_equations_p: Solve equations with 1-4 variables, from basic to advanced systems
word_problems_p: Real-world math applications and story problems
house_problems_p: Find missing numbers on house roofs - great for young learners
pyramid_problems_p: Build pyramids by adding numbers layer by layer
simplify_equations_p: Simplify algebraic expressions with brackets and variables.
simplify_rationals_p: Simplify rational expressions by canceling common factors.
number_sequences_p: Find the next term in a sequence (arithmetic, geometric, squares, Fibonacci-like).
operator_puzzles_p: Fill in the missing operators (and brackets, if enabled) to make the equation true.
compare_expressions_p: Fill in <, >, or = between two expressions. Quick mental-math drill.
boolean_logic_p: Evaluate logical expressions (∧ ∨ ¬ → ↔) given true/false values for each variable.
unit_conversion_p: Convert, add and subtract lengths, masses, volumes, times and money.
time_calendar_p: Clock times, durations, timetables, weekdays and dates as short story problems.
find_the_number_p: Number riddles: numbers described in words, "I think of a number" chains, halving chains and linked letter equations.
combinatorics_p: List and count all possibilities: menus, choosing, arranging, handshakes, half-time scores, dominoes.
integer_solutions_p: Search problems: legs, vertices, market prices, notes, numbers with a given sum, matchstick squares, even and odd pairs.
number_properties_p: Number riddles: remainders, digit sums and products, counting, consecutive numbers, palindromes, primes.
grid_figures_p: Perimeter, area and corners of figures made of squares, staircases, glued squares, comparing figures.

templates.age1: {name1} is {multiplier} times as old as {name2}. The sum of their ages is {sum}. How old is {name1}?
templates.age2: {name1} is {diff} years older than {name2}. In {years} years, {name1} will be {multiplier} times as old as {name2}. How old is {name1} now?
templates.age3: The sum of two consecutive integers is {sum}. Find the larger number.
templates.age4: {name1} is {age1} years old. {name2} is {diff} years younger. What is the sum of their ages?
templates.age5: In {years} years, {name1} will be {final_age} years old. How old is {name1} now?
templates.distance1: A car travels {distance} miles in {time} hours. What is the car's speed in miles per hour?
templates.distance2: Two cars start from the same point. One travels north at {speed1} mph, the other south at {speed2} mph. After {time} hours, how far apart are they?
templates.distance3: A train travels {distance1} miles in the morning and {distance2} miles in the afternoon. If the total trip took {time} hours, what was the average speed?
templates.distance4: {name} walks {speed} miles per hour. How long does it take to walk {distance} miles?
templates.distance5: Two trains start {distance} miles apart and travel toward each other at {speed1} mph and {speed2} mph. When will they meet?
templates.money1: Tickets cost ${adult_price} for adults and ${child_price} for children. If {total_tickets} tickets were sold for ${total_money}, how many adult tickets were sold?
templates.money2: A store sells {item1} for ${price1} each and {item2} for ${price2} each. If you buy {total_items} items for ${total_cost}, how many {item1} did you buy?
templates.money3: {name} has ${amount} in quarters and dimes. If there are {total_coins} coins total, how many quarters are there?
templates.money4: A restaurant bill is ${bill}. If you want to leave a {percent}% tip, how much tip should you leave?
templates.money5: {name} saves ${amount} per week. How much will be saved in {weeks} weeks?
templates.work1: {name1} can complete a job in {time1} hours. {name2} can complete the same job in {time2} hours. How long would it take them working together?
templates.work2: Pipe A can fill a pool in {time1} hours. Pipe B can fill it in {time2} hours. How long to fill the pool with both pipes open?
templates.work3: {name} can paint {rooms} rooms in {time} hours. At this rate, how long to paint {new_rooms} rooms?
templates.work4: A factory produces {items} items per hour. How many items are produced in {time} hours?
templates.mixture1: How many gallons of {percent1}% solution must be mixed with {gallons} gallons of {percent2}% solution to get {target_percent}% solution?
templates.mixture2: A {percent1}% acid solution is mixed with a {percent2}% acid solution. If {total_volume} liters of {final_percent}% solution is needed, how many liters of each solution should be mixed?
templates.mixture3: Coffee worth ${price1} per pound is mixed with coffee worth ${price2} per pound. How many pounds of each should be used to make {total_pounds} pounds worth ${avg_price} per pound?
templates.mixture4: A {percent}% salt solution weighs {weight} pounds. How many pounds of pure salt does it contain?
templates.geometry1: A rectangle's length is {diff} cm more than its width. If the perimeter is {perimeter} cm, find the width.
templates.geometry2: A triangle has sides of {side1} cm, {side2} cm, and {side3} cm. What is its perimeter?
templates.geometry3: A square has a perimeter of {perimeter} cm. What is the length of each side?
templates.geometry4: A circle has a radius of {radius} cm. What is its area? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
templates.number1: One number is {diff} more than another. Their sum is {sum}. Find the larger number.
templates.number2: The product of two consecutive even integers is {product}. Find the integers.
templates.number3: Three consecutive odd integers sum to {sum}. Find the middle integer.
templates.number4: If you multiply a number by {multiplier} and add {addition}, you get {result}. What is the number?
templates.percent4: A shirt originally costs ${original_price}. It's on sale for {percent}% off. What is the sale price?
templates.oly1: Liam is {diff} years older than Mia. Mia is {mult} times as old as Jack. Jack is {young} years old. How old is Liam?
templates.oly2: Ben and Jack are {sum} years old together. Jack is {diff} years younger than Ben. How old is Ben?
templates.oly3: Jack is {older} and his sister is {younger}. In how many years will Jack be {mult} times as old as his sister?
templates.oly4: There were {total} cookies on a plate. Lily took 1/{a} of them, Kate took 1/{b} of the rest, and Sam took 1/{c} of what remained. How many cookies are left on the plate?
templates.oly5: In a hall, 1/{k} of the seats are taken by children, {adults} seats by adults, and {free} seats are free. How many seats are there in the hall?
templates.oly6: A rope {length} m long was cut into three parts. The mother got half as much as her son, and the daughter got {mult} times as much as the mother. How many metres did the daughter get?
templates.oly7: Ann, Bob, Carl, Dan and Eva collect stamps. Bob has half as many stamps as Dan. Eva has {more} more stamps than Bob. Carl has as many as Eva. Ann has as many as Bob and Carl together. Together they have {total} stamps. How many stamps does Dan have?
templates.oly8: Tom said to Max: “If you give me {k} marbles, I will have {q} times as many as you. If I give you {k} marbles, we will have the same number.” How many marbles does Tom have?
templates.oly9: In a class, {football} pupils play football and {swim} pupils swim; {both} of them do both, and {neither} do neither. How many pupils are in the class?
templates.oly10: Points A, B, C and E lie on a line in this order. AE = {ae} cm, segment BE is {q} times as long as AB, and AC is {bc} cm longer than AB. How long is CE in cm?
templates.oly11: Grandma is handing out sweets to her grandchildren. If she gives each of them {a}, {left} are left over. If she gives each of them {b}, she is {short} short. How many grandchildren does she have?
templates.oly12: Find the missing number so that the average of {nums} and the missing number is {avg}.

house_problems.description: Find the missing number on each house roof. The number in the middle is the sum of the two numbers on the sides.

house_problems.error_max_problems: Max 50 problems for this format. Please choose a smaller number.

pyramid_problems.description: Add adjacent numbers in each layer to build the pyramid. Each stone contains the sum of the two stones below it.
pyramid_problems.error_invalid_num_problems: Please enter a valid Number of Problems (>= 1).
pyramid_problems.error_max_problems: Max 20 problems for this format. Please choose a smaller number.

simplify_equations.description: Simplify algebraic expressions by combining like terms. Configure the number of operations, whether to include brackets, and the coefficient range. The control sum is the digital root of |a| + |b|.
simplify_equations.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Simplify to ax + b, then find the digital root of |a| + |b|.

simplify_rationals.description: Simplify rational expressions by canceling common factors. Pick which problem forms to include and set the maximum coefficient that appears in the unsimplified fraction. The control sum is the digital root of the simplified numerator and denominator coefficients.
simplify_rationals.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Find the digital root of the sum of simplified numerator and denominator coefficients.

boolean_logic.description: Each problem is a nested logical expression with assigned truth values. Decide whether the whole expression is true or false.
boolean_logic.print_instructions: Substitute the values, evaluate the expression, and write T (true) or F (false).
boolean_logic.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Count the sub-expressions (every bracketed group and every ¬) that come out true. Take the last digit of that count and compare to the cell.

compare_expressions.description: Fill in <, >, or = between the two expressions. About a quarter of problems are intentionally engineered as equalities to keep the answer mix varied.
compare_expressions.print_instructions: Compute each side, then write <, >, or = between them.
compare_expressions.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Take the larger of the two sides (either if equal). Find its digital root and compare to the cell.

operator_puzzles.description: Fill in the missing operators ( +, −, × ) so the equation matches the given target. Enable brackets to require some problems to use parentheses; enable operand-blank to mix in puzzles where one number is missing instead.

number_sequences.description: Find the next term in each sequence. Pick which sequence types to include, the number of visible terms, and the maximum allowed value. Enable negatives for arithmetic differences and alternating geometric ratios.
number_sequences.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Find the digital root of the next term (use absolute value if negative).

script.invalid_num_problems_alert: Please enter a valid number of problems.

time_calendar.type_calendar_label: Calendar (weekdays, dates, day of the year)
time_calendar.description: Short story problems about clock time and the calendar. Times are written on a 24-hour clock.
time_calendar.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Take the digital root of a number made from your answer: a time of day → minutes since midnight (9:15 → 555); a duration → total minutes (2 h 30 min → 150); a weekday → its number (Monday 1 … Sunday 7); a date → its day of the year (1 February → 32); a count → the number itself.
time_calendar.error_message: Error generating time problems. Select at least one problem type.

templates.clock_after: It is {from} now. What time will it be in {duration}?
templates.clock_between: How many hours and minutes pass from {from} to {to}?

templates.timeline_arrival: {name} leaves home at {start}, {legs}. At what time does {name} arrive?
templates.timeline_total: {name} leaves home at {start}, {legs}. How long does the whole trip take?

templates.weekday_ago: Today is {weekday}. What day of the week was it {days} ago?
templates.weekday_ahead: Today is {weekday}. What day of the week will it be in {days}?

templates.hotel: {name} spends the first night at a hotel on {date1} and stays {nights}. On what date does {name} leave?

templates.days_between: How many days pass from {date1} to {date2}?

templates.age_days_years: {name} is {n_days} old. How many full years is that? (Count 365 days in a year.)

templates.age_days_weeks: A kitten is {n_days} old. How many full weeks is that?

find_the_number.description: Olympiad-style riddles. Work backwards from the result to the hidden number.
find_the_number.letters_instruction: Find a, then b, then c. Write down c.
find_the_number.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Write the digital root of each number you found (for letter equations: of c).
find_the_number.error_message: Error generating problems. Select at least one problem type.
find_the_number.describe_compound: Calculate {x} and {y}. {outer} Which number do you get?

outer.sub: Then subtract the second result from the first.
outer.div: Then divide the first result by the second.

find_the_number.inverse_template: I think of a number, {steps} and get {result}. What is my number?
find_the_number.halving_template: {name} has some {items} and gives {gives}. In the end, {name} keeps {kept}. How many {items_count} did {name} have at the start?

halving_steps.first_plus: half of them and one more to {to}
halving_steps.rest: then half of the rest to {to}
halving_steps.rest_plus: then half of the rest and one more to {to}

combinatorics.type_choose_label: Choose some of them (order does not matter)
combinatorics.type_arrange_label: Arrange in a row (PINs, apps, coloured cards)
combinatorics.description: Counting problems: write down every possibility in a system, then count them. A lower largest answer keeps the lists short.
combinatorics.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Take the digital root of each count.
combinatorics.error_message: Error generating counting problems. Select at least one problem type.
combinatorics.list_prompt: Write down all possibilities. How many are there?

templates.product_menu: A café has a lunch menu — {groups}. A lunch is one dish from each group.
templates.product_outfit: {name} has these clothes — {groups}. An outfit is one item of each kind.
templates.choose_friends: {name} may invite {k} of the friends {items} to the cinema.
templates.choose_toppings: A pizza gets {k} different toppings out of {items}.
templates.choose_flavours: An ice-cream cup holds {k} scoops of different flavours, chosen from {items}.
templates.arrange_apps: {name} puts the apps {items} in one row on the phone screen.

templates.arrange_first: {name} puts the apps {items} in one row on the phone screen, and {first} must be first.

templates.tournament: {n} teams play a tournament: each team plays each other team once.

templates.halftime_second: A football match ended {a}:{b}, and the number of goals scored in the second half was {k}. What could the score have been at half-time?

integer_solutions.type_subset_label: Choose numbers with a given sum
integer_solutions.description: Search problems: try the possibilities in order and write down every solution.
integer_solutions.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Problems that ask for all solutions: write the number of solutions. Other problems: the digital root of the number the problem asks for.
integer_solutions.error_message: Error generating search problems. Select at least one problem type.
integer_solutions.find_all: Find all solutions. Self-check: how many solutions are there?

templates.legs_count: There are chickens and sheep in a yard, {n} animals in all. Together they have {legs} legs. How many sheep are there?
templates.legs_all: Chickens and sheep in a yard have {legs} legs in all, and there is at least one of each. How many chickens and how many sheep can there be?

templates.vertices: Some squares and some pentagons are drawn on a sheet, at least one of each. Together they have {v} vertices. How many squares and how many pentagons can there be?
templates.market_count: At a market a cow costs {p1} €, a goat {p2} € and a hen {p3} €. A farmer spent exactly 100 € and bought exactly {n} animals, at least one of each kind. How many cows, goats and hens did he buy? Self-check: the number of hens.
templates.market_most: At a market a cow costs {p1} €, a goat {p2} € and a hen {p3} €. A farmer spends exactly 100 € and buys at least one animal of each kind. What is the largest number of animals he can buy?

templates.money_fewest: Pay exactly {a} € using only notes of 200 €, 100 € and 20 €. What is the smallest number of notes you need?
templates.money_most: Pay exactly {a} € using only notes of 200 €, 100 € and 20 €. What is the largest number of notes you can use?
templates.note_coins: In a pocket there is one {note} € note and three equal coins. A coin can be {coins}. What can the money in the pocket add up to?
templates.notes_three: A wallet holds exactly three notes, and at least one of them is 5 €. Each note is 5 €, 10 €, 20 € or 50 €, and together they are worth less than {l} €. Which amounts can be in the wallet?

templates.parity_pick: The natural numbers a and b add up to {t}, a is even and b is odd. Write down all such pairs, then find the pair with {c1}·a + {c2}·b = {w}. Self-check: the number a.

number_properties.type_count_label: How many numbers have the property?
number_properties.type_consecutive_label: Consecutive numbers with a given sum
number_properties.type_extremes_label: Smallest and largest numbers, next palindrome
number_properties.description: Number riddles about remainders, digits, palindromes and primes. Each riddle has exactly one answer.
number_properties.digit_terms_hint: The digit sum of a number is the sum of its digits, the digit product is the product of its digits: for 352 the digit sum is 3 + 5 + 2 = 10 and the digit product is 3 · 5 · 2 = 30.
number_properties.palindrome_hint: A palindrome is a number that reads the same from left to right and from right to left, for example 373.
number_properties.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Write the digital root of the answer. For problems asking for all ways, write the number of ways.
number_properties.error_message: Error generating number riddles. Select at least one problem type.

templates.remainder: I am thinking of a natural number less than {max}. Which number is it?
templates.digits_2: I am thinking of a two-digit number. Which number is it?
templates.digits_3: I am thinking of a three-digit number. Which number is it?
templates.cond_remainder: Divided by {a}, it leaves the remainder {r}.
templates.cond_pred_divisible: The number before it is divisible by {k}.
templates.cond_succ_divisible: The number after it is divisible by {k}.
templates.cond_between: It is greater than {lo} and less than {hi}.
templates.cond_tens_times_ones: Its tens digit is {k} times its ones digit.
templates.cond_increasing: Its digits get larger from left to right.
templates.cond_first_last: Its first and last digits are the same.
templates.count_digit_sum: How many numbers from {a} to {b} have the digit sum {s}?
templates.count_palindromes_digit: How many three-digit palindromes contain the digit {d}?
templates.count_palindromes_range: How many palindromes are there between {a} and {b}?
templates.consecutive: The sum of {k} consecutive natural numbers is {s}. What is the smallest of these numbers?
templates.consecutive_step: There are {k} natural numbers, each {d} greater than the one before. Their sum is {s}. What is the smallest of these numbers?
templates.smallest_sum: What is the smallest three-digit number with the digit sum {s}?
templates.largest_sum: What is the largest three-digit number with the digit sum {s}?
templates.largest_less: What is the largest three-digit number whose digit sum is less than {s}?
templates.distinct_digit_sum: A {k}-digit number has all different digits. What is the largest digit sum it can have?
templates.next_palindrome: {p} is a palindrome. What is the next palindrome after {p}, and how much larger is it? Self-check: the next palindrome.
templates.prime_sum: Write {n} as the sum of two prime numbers in all possible ways. Self-check: the number of ways.
templates.prime_count: How many prime numbers are there between {a} and {b}?

grid_figures.type_perimeter_label: Perimeter of a figure on squared paper
grid_figures.type_corners_label: Number of corners of a figure
grid_figures.type_compare_label: Compare figures: largest area or perimeter
grid_figures.halves_label: Area: allow half squares (cut along a diagonal)
grid_figures.description: Figures made of squares on squared paper. In print every square of a figure is exactly one square of the paper.
grid_figures.control_sum_grid_subtitle: Write the digital root of the answer (for a letter: A = 1, B = 2, C = 3). If an area has half squares, use the double area.
grid_figures.error_message: Error generating figure problems. Select at least one problem type.

templates.perimeter: Each square of the grid has a side of 1 cm. What is the perimeter of the grey figure?
templates.area: What is the area of the grey figure? Count it in grid squares.
templates.area_halves: What is the area of the grey figure in grid squares? A square cut along its diagonal counts as half a square. Self-check: use the double area.
templates.corners: How many corners does the grey figure have?
templates.staircase_perimeter: The figure is a staircase with {k} equal steps. It is {W} cm wide and {H} cm high. The drawing is not to scale. What is the perimeter of the figure?
templates.staircase_step: The figure is a staircase with {k} equal steps. It is {W} cm wide and {H} cm high. The drawing is not to scale. How high is one step?
templates.glued_intro: Squares {names} are glued together as in the picture. The drawing is not to scale.
templates.glued_given: Square {s} has a perimeter of {p} cm.
templates.glued_width: The whole figure is {l} cm wide.
templates.glued_height: The whole figure is {l} cm high.
templates.glued_side: What is the side of square {s}?
templates.glued_perimeter: What is the perimeter of the whole figure?
templates.compare_area: Which figure has the largest area? Write its letter.
templates.compare_perimeter: Each square of the grid has a side of 1 cm. Which figure has the largest perimeter? Write its letter.
